categories.name: ANAGRAMS
categories.note: Rearrange the letters of the word in capitals to get the response

clues.text: Rearrange LISTEN to get this word for making no noise
Rearrange EARTH to get this organ that pumps your blood
The letters of DORMITORY rearrange into this two-word description of a messy bedroom
The letters of ASTRONOMER rearrange into this two-word phrase for someone gazing at the night sky
The letters of THE EYES rearrange into this two-word phrase for what they do

categories.name: SOUNDS THE SAME
categories.note: Each clue names a word; the response is its homophone, a word that sounds the same but is spelled differently

clues.text: A homophone of "flour", it is the blooming part of a plant
A homophone of "stationary", it is the paper and envelopes you write letters on
A homophone of "principle", it is the head of a school
A homophone of "cymbal", it is a sign or mark that stands for something else
A homophone of "colonel", it is the soft part inside the shell of a nut

categories.name: BORROWED WORDS
categories.note: English words taken from other languages

clues.text: This German word meaning "children's garden" is a grade in Canadian schools
From the French for "already seen", the feeling that you have lived through a moment before
This Japanese word meaning "empty orchestra" is singing along to a recorded backing track
From Yiddish, this word means shameless nerve or audacity
This German word means taking pleasure in someone else's misfortune

categories.name: IDIOMS
categories.note: Fill in the missing word of a common expression

clues.text: Something very easy to do is "a piece of" this dessert
To give away a secret is to spill these
Someone pursuing a mistaken idea is "barking up the wrong" one of these
When it pours, it is raining these two animals
Someone stuck in a bad spot with no way out is "up the creek without" one of these

categories.name: CANADIANISMS
categories.note: Words and phrases heard mostly in Canada

clues.text: This one-dollar coin is nicknamed for the bird on its face
The Canadian word for a knitted winter hat that Americans might call a beanie
In Canadian slang, a case of 24 beers is called this, hyphenated
In much of Canada the electricity bill is called this, after the dams that generate the power
This old-fashioned Canadian word for a sofa is also the name of a market town in Derbyshire, England

categories.name: PALINDROMES
categories.note: Every response reads the same backwards and forwards

clues.text: Twelve o'clock in the daytime
A narrow boat paddled with a double-bladed paddle
A system that spots planes and ships with radio waves
A principle or belief held firmly, as by a religion or a political party
The spinning blade assembly on top of a helicopter

categories.name: HIDDEN ANIMALS
categories.note: Every response is a word with an animal's name hidden inside it

clues.text: A list of products for sale, often mailed to your home, hides a feline
A substance that gives colour, such as the melanin in skin, hides a farm animal
A small pointed beard on the chin hides a horned animal
A set of beliefs laid down by an authority as beyond question hides man's best friend
An angry or bad-tempered frown hides a bird of the night

categories.name: PORTMANTEAUS
categories.note: Every response is a word blended from two other words

clues.text: Breakfast plus lunch
Smoke plus fog
Web plus log, an online journal
Spoon plus fork, a piece of camping cutlery
Lewis Carroll blended "chuckle" and "snort" into this word in "Through the Looking-Glass"

categories.name: SPELLING BEE
categories.note: Spell the word described; the spelling must be exact

clues.text: A word meaning apart or distinct, often misspelled with an E in the middle instead of an A
A word meaning essential or required, with one C and two S's
To make someone feel awkward or ashamed, with two R's and two S's
To provide lodging or make room for, with two C's and two M's
A repeated pattern of beats in music or poetry, spelled with no A, E, I, O or U

categories.name: A GROUP EFFORT
categories.note: Every response is the collective noun for a group of the animals named

clues.text: A group of lions
A group of fish swimming together
A group of geese on the ground
A group of crows, with a grim name
A group of owls, named as if they were lawmakers

categories.name: FEAR ITSELF
categories.note: Each clue names a phobia; the response is what it is a fear of

clues.text: Arachnophobia
Acrophobia
Nyctophobia
Triskaidekaphobia
Ophidiophobia

categories.name: LATIN LESSONS
categories.note: Latin phrases still used in English

clues.text: Meaning "and the rest", it is usually shortened to etc.
"Seize the day"
Meaning "in good faith", it describes something genuine or real
Julius Caesar's three-word boast meaning "I came, I saw, I conquered"
Literally "you shall have the body", this legal order requires a prisoner to be brought before a court

final.text: Sir Thomas More coined this word in 1516 from Greek roots meaning "no place" as the title of his book about an ideal island society
